title: AI assistant integration
description: Give your assistant the API documentation and role-based access.
markdown: ## Read the API documentation Give your AI assistant the [documentation index](https://www.musedam.cc/en-US/developers/llms.txt), the [Product Library quick start in Markdown](https://www.musedam.cc/en-US/developers/markdown/product-library.md), and the [OpenAPI contract](/assets/developers/product-library/openapi.json). The page toolbar can copy a ready-to-use prompt or the current document as Markdown. These resources are public and do not require repository access. > Read the Product Library quick start and API documentation before implementation. Use https://open.musedam.cc/api/product as the API Base URL. Determine the required collaborator role from the requested operation, and use only documented endpoints and fields. For synchronization, follow the cursor protocol and reconcile visibility. Keep credentials in secure local or server-side configuration. ## Configure credentials and permissions Use an existing MuseDAM API key. Ask a Product Library Manager to add it as an API Key Collaborator through **Member Settings → Add Members**. Its initial role is `view_only`; choose a role for the intended operations. Product Library does not issue keys, and each role defines its operation permissions. Send the API key in the `Authorization: Bearer ` header from your server. See [getting access](./product-library#authentication-and-scope). ## Choose the relevant guide - Read the [API documentation](./product-library-reference) for parameters and response schemas. - Follow [write conventions](./product-library-write-conventions) for idempotency and concurrent changes. - Use [product synchronization](./product-library-synchronization) for catalog copies and checkpoints. - Adapt the [curl examples](./product-library-examples) to the intended operation. Creation, publication, sharing and deletion affect real team data.

title: Product Library examples
description: Use standalone curl examples to read, create, publish, share, download and synchronize products.
markdown: Use each example independently. Replace `your_api_key` with your API key and the example resource IDs with IDs from your Product Library. ## List products Add the key as an API Key Collaborator first. See [getting access](./product-library#authentication-and-scope). This request lists products visible to the current role. ```bash curl --request GET 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/products?page=1&pageSize=20' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' ``` Read products from `data` and paging information from `pagination`. The `view_only` and `usable` roles can only read published products. ## Create brands, categories and templates Creating a brand requires the `manage` role. ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/brands' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{"name":"Example brand"}' ``` The response returns the brand ID in `data.id`. See [product categories](./product-library-categories) and [product information templates](./product-library-template-writes) for their creation parameters. Reuse existing resources when they already meet your needs. ## Find assets Find an existing image before creating or editing a product. This endpoint requires `editable` or `manage`. ```bash curl --request GET 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/assets?mimeType=image%2F&pageSize=20' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' ``` Use the returned asset `id` in `coverAssetId` or `imageAssetIds`. Use `previewUrl` to display a preview. ## Create a product Creating a product requires `editable` or `manage`. This example uses brand `10`, category `20` within that brand and image asset `30`. Replace these with existing resource IDs. ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/products' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Idempotency-Key: create-product-001' \ --data-raw '{"name":"Example product","spu":"EXAMPLE-001","brandId":10,"categoryId":20,"coverAssetId":30,"imageAssetIds":[30]}' ``` The new product is a draft. Read its ID from `data.id`. When retrying the same creation, keep the request body and `Idempotency-Key` unchanged. Use a new idempotency key to create another product. ## Update and publish a product Update the description of product `40`: ```bash curl --request PATCH 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/products/40' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{"description":"New product description"}' ``` Omitted fields keep their values. Send `null` to clear a nullable field or `[]` to clear a media list. To prevent overwriting concurrent changes, send the `ETag` returned by a read in the `If-Match` header. See [writes and error handling](./product-library-write-conventions). Publish product `40`: ```bash curl --request PATCH 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/products/40/status' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{"status":"published"}' ``` Fill the template’s required fields and make sure its assets are available before publishing. Validation failures return `422` with field details and leave the product unchanged. ## Read product details and previews Read the details of product `40`: ```bash curl --request GET 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/products/40' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' ``` Display product media with `previewUrl`. With download permission, media may also include `downloadUrl` and `downloadUrlExpiresAt`. Read the product again when a link expires. ## Share, export and download Create a seven-day share for published product `40`, with downloads disabled. This requires `usable` or higher: ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/product-shares' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{"productIds":[40],"expiresInDays":7,"allowDownload":false}' ``` The share URL is returned in `data.url`. Export product `40` to Excel. This requires `usable` or higher: ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/product-downloads' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{"kind":"export","productIds":[40],"format":"xlsx","includeAssetUrls":false}' \ --output 'products.xlsx' ``` The example saves `products.xlsx` without asset links. The `format` field also supports `csv` and `json`. Download the original files for product `40`. This requires `usable` or higher: ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/product-downloads' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{"kind":"assets","productIds":[40]}' \ --output 'product-download' ``` The result is saved as `product-download`. A single file is returned in its original format; multiple files are returned as a ZIP. Adjust the filename for the returned file type. ## Understand product template versions A product saves the template version used at creation. Later template edits or deletion do not change that product’s field definitions. Read that version from `templateDefinition` in the product details. See [product information templates](./product-library-template-writes). ## Synchronize products Start the first synchronization with this request: ```bash curl --request GET 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/products?sync=true&pageSize=100' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' ``` If `pagination.nextCursor` is not `null`, replace `your_cursor` below with its complete value to fetch the next page: ```bash curl --get 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/products' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --data-urlencode 'sync=true' \ --data-urlencode 'cursor=your_cursor' ``` Continue with each returned `nextCursor` until it is `null`, even when a page has an empty `data` array. After processing every page, save `pagination.syncedUntil` unchanged. In the next cycle, pass it as `updatedAfter` in the first request. Keep the timestamp’s full precision. See [product synchronization](./product-library-synchronization) for the complete rules. ## Check product visibility Synchronization does not return records for deleted products. Periodically check product IDs stored locally: ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/product/products/visibility' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{"ids":[40,41]}' ``` Remove products reported as `not_visible` from your local copy. This status can also mean a draft is hidden or access is unavailable; it does not establish whether a product exists. To delete a product itself, see [product writes and publishing](./product-library-product-writes). ## Handle common errors | Status | Action | | --- | --- | | 401 / 403 | Check the API key status and collaborator role. | | 412 | Read the product again, review the changes and retry with the new ETag. | | 422 | Fix the parameters identified by `details[].field` and `details[].message`. | | 409 | Handle the conflict using `code`. For `mutation_response_unavailable`, read and verify the result first. | Keep the response `requestId` for troubleshooting. See the complete [error codes](./product-library-write-conventions#error-catalog).

title: Writes and error handling
description: Handle idempotent retries, ETags, brand writes and committed write failures.

headings.title: Update only the fields you need
Check whether a write took effect
Find an error and its next step

markdown:
## Read before updating To avoid overwriting another change to a product, brand, category or template: 1. Read the resource and save the response `ETag`, including its quotes. 2. Send that value in `If-Match` when using PATCH, changing status or deleting. 3. If the response is `412 precondition_failed`, read again, reconcile the changes and retry with the new ETag. `If-Match` is optional. Without it, the last write wins. Shares, history and recorded downloads do not use ETag or If-Match. All requests use `https://open.musedam.cc/api/product`. Access depends on the current API Key Collaborator role. A team, library, actor or operation allowlist in the request cannot grant additional access.
ETag matching and validity - Catalog item reads and successful mutations return a strong, quoted ETag. Pass it unchanged; do not generate one yourself. - `*` or a comma-separated list containing the current strong ETag also matches. Weak tags do not. Stale or weak tags return 412 without changing the resource. - `If-None-Match` and 304 responses are not supported. - Template groups, fields, bindings and library defaults all affect the ETag. Removal or movement invalidates the old tag. - Asset ETags depend on the file-path and linked-asset identities and update timestamps. Persistent metadata changes update the tag; refreshing a temporary preview signature alone does not.
## Retry an uncertain create Resource creation returns 201. Add an optional `Idempotency-Key` when you need safe retries: 1. Assign a key to one create operation. 2. If the outcome is uncertain, retry within 24 hours with **the same key and input**. 3. Use a new key to create another resource. Different input under the same key returns `409 idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are scoped to the team, API key and create operation. Use a nonblank value of at most 255 characters, without ASCII control characters.
Can the data returned by a retry change? - Matching canonical input replays the first successful non-media result and ETag, even if the resource was later edited. - Media URLs are issued again after checking current access, visibility and associations. Signed URLs are never saved as replay credentials. - Products retain only original media IDs whose associations remain valid in their original slots. Later additions are excluded, and removed downloads are not restored. - A replay cannot restore deleted or currently invisible products.
## Update only the fields you need | Request content | Behavior | | --- | --- | | Omitted field | Preserves its current value | | Explicit `null` | Clears only a nullable field | | Product `templateFields` | Shallow-merges by custom field ID; `null` clears that value | | Template `groups` | Replaces the full definition; preserve existing group and field IDs, including protected system fields | Unknown JSON properties are rejected. See [product writes](./product-library-product-writes) and [template writes](./product-library-template-writes) for individual fields. ## Brand write requirements Brand writes require the `manage` role. Create accepts `name`, `description` and `logoUrl`; PATCH must include at least one of them. | Field | Requirement | | --- | --- | | `name` | Nonempty after trimming, at most 128 characters; duplicates allowed | | `description` | Nullable, at most 512 characters | | `logoUrl` | An allowed storage/CDN host and HTTP(S) URL without embedded credentials | A brand cannot be deleted while a nondeleted category or product references it. Reassign or remove those dependencies first.
Brand codes, logos and response fields - The server generates `code`, unique within the library. Clients cannot set it. Exhausted code conflicts return `409 code_in_use`. - Logo query signatures are removed before storage. Writes reference a URL; they do not upload or remotely import an asset. - Brand responses omit `logoUrl`. They return `id`, `name`, `code`, `description`, `website`, `sortOrder`, `isEnabled`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`.
## Check whether a write took effect Before retrying an error, check the write outcome. | Response | Next step | | --- | --- | | `503 write_conflict` | The write rolled back. Wait for `Retry-After: 1`, then retry with the original create key; reread any stale ETag | | `409 mutation_response_unavailable` | The write committed or was replayed. Reconcile through an authorized read or the original key to avoid duplicate creation | | A download or export error with `mutationOutcome` | The business record committed or was replayed. Keep the original key when retrying the accepted operation |
Response preparation failures and download status If a write takes effect but its response cannot be prepared, it returns `success: false`, `data: null` and `mutationOutcome: committed` (or `replayed`). No ETag or media URL is returned. The write was not rolled back. Downloads and exports retain their specific preparation or delivery error code. `requested` means the request was accepted, not that transfer finished or a file was saved locally.
## Investigate a failed request 1. Look up the HTTP status and `code` below. Do not identify error types by the `message` text. 2. For validation failures, inspect `details[].field` and correct the input. 3. Provide `X-Request-Id` or the JSON `requestId` when seeking help. Do not log credentials or signed media URLs. ## Find an error and its next step Expand the group matching the response status.
Authentication and access: 401, 403, 404, 503 | Status / code | Next step | | --- | --- | | 401 `invalid_credentials` | The Bearer key is missing, malformed or unknown. Check the header and key | | 401 `key_inactive` | The key is disabled, revoked or expired. Use an active key | | 403 `forbidden` | Check the current collaborator role and permissions for the operation or published state | | 404 `not_found` | Check the ID and visibility. Missing, deleted, other-library and invisible resources can all produce this error; do not infer existence | | 503 `authentication_unavailable` | Live authentication is unavailable. Retry later; no protected operation runs for this request |
Input and request size: 413, 422 | Status / code | Next step | | --- | --- | | 413 `payload_too_large` | Reduce the request body to at most 1 MiB (1048576 bytes) | | 422 `validation_failed` | Check query parameters, body, references and field state; use `details` when provided |
Duplicates and dependencies: 409 | Code | Next step | | --- | --- | | `sku_in_use` | Change the nonempty product `spu` that is already in use | | `code_in_use` | The generated brand code conflicted. Retry creation | | `name_in_use` | Choose another template name or sibling category name | | `brand_has_dependents` | Remove or reassign nondeleted categories and products under the brand | | `category_has_products` | Resolve nondeleted products in the category subtree first | | `default_template_replacement_required` | Supply a replacement template ID or explicit `null` |
Retries and write outcomes: 409, 412, 500, 503 | Status / code | Next step | | --- | --- | | 409 `idempotency_key_reused` | Canonical input differs for the same key. Keep the original input for a retry; use a new key for a new operation | | 409 `mutation_response_unavailable` | The change committed or was replayed. Reconcile before retrying | | 412 `precondition_failed` | Reread, reconcile and retry with the current ETag | | 500 `internal_server_error` | Preserve `requestId` for investigation; internal details are not exposed | | 503 `write_conflict` | The write rolled back. Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry with the original key |
File downloads: 409, 413 | Status / code | Next step | | --- | --- | | 409 `download_unavailable` | The original cannot be prepared. Recheck download-candidate availability | | 413 `download_too_large` | Reduce the selection to at most 200 files and 500 MiB combined |
## Request count and size limits | Applies to | Limit | | --- | --- | | Bodies on all routes, including reads | 1 MiB (1048576 bytes); larger bodies return 413 | | Ordinary or synchronization pages | Default 20, maximum 100; larger values are capped at 100 | | Idempotency records | Retained for 24 hours |
Product, template and category limits | Applies to | Limit | | --- | --- | | Media references in one product write | 100 total across cover, images, related assets and custom fields | | Template definition | 200 fields total, 1–200 groups | | Template binding arrays | At most 10000 IDs per dimension | | Category tree | Depth 10, at most 5000 nondeleted nodes per brand | | Visibility check | 0–100 IDs; duplicates and order are preserved | | Synchronization cursor | Opaque string, at most 8192 characters |
Share, download and export limits | Applies to | Limit | | --- | --- | | Products per share, download or export | 1–100 | | Files per original download | At most 200 | | Original download size | At most 500 MiB combined |
v1 defines no 429 or rate-limit contract. Write contention uses `503 write_conflict`. Multipart uploads, remote asset imports, generic provider synchronization, webhooks and bulk writes are not available. UI operations retain their own workflows.

title: Product categories
description: Read category trees, change hierarchy and ordering, and delete subtrees.

headings.title: Delete a category and its children

markdown: `GET /api/product/categories` lists live categories, with optional `brandId`, `page`, and `pageSize` filters. Results are flat so clients can build their own hierarchy from `id`, `parentId`, and `brandId`. Ordering is stable by brand, parent, sibling position, and ID. `GET /categories/{id}` returns one live category and its strong `ETag`. Both endpoints require `categories:read`. Library scope always comes from the API key; caller-supplied tenant IDs do not change it. Missing, foreign, and deleted item IDs return `404 not_found`. `POST /categories`, `PATCH /categories/{id}`, and `DELETE /categories/{id}` require the `manage` role and the matching create, update or delete permission. Follow [writes and error handling](./product-library-write-conventions): use `If-Match` to check for concurrent changes and `Idempotency-Key` to retry creation safely within 24 hours. ## Fields and tree rules Create accepts required `brandId` and `name`, plus optional `parentId`, `sortOrder`, `description`, `iconEmoji`, `iconAssetId`, and `isEnabled`. PATCH accepts a nonempty subset of those optional fields and `name`. `brandId` cannot be changed after creation. Unknown fields, including caller-supplied paths or actor IDs, are rejected. - Names retain their exact spelling, must contain non-whitespace text, are limited to 64 characters, and cannot contain `/`. Exact duplicate sibling names return `409 name_in_use`; different parents or brands may reuse names. - Parents must be live categories in the same brand and library. The brand must also belong to the key's library. Cycles, invalid references, more than 10 category levels, and more than 5000 live nodes per brand return `422 validation_failed`. - `sortOrder` is a zero-based position in the destination sibling group. Omission appends a new or moved category; an update within the same parent preserves its position. Insertion and movement renumber affected siblings. Positions beyond the sibling count return `422 validation_failed`. - Names and parent changes recompute descendant paths without changing IDs. Affected categories record the API operator and an updated timestamp. - `description`, `iconEmoji`, and `iconAssetId` may be cleared with `null`. Emoji text is limited to 16 characters. An icon asset must belong to the current library. `isEnabled` defaults to true on create. On creation, the library default template is explicitly bound to the new category only if the template has no brand bindings or includes the category's brand. This direct binding takes precedence over ancestor bindings. Otherwise, creation succeeds without an explicit category binding; template resolution still checks ancestors, then the brand, then the library default. Responses contain `id`, `brandId`, `parentId`, `name`, `pathKey`, `description`, `iconEmoji`, `iconAssetId`, `sortOrder`, `isEnabled`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`. `pathKey` is server-owned and starts with `/`. No icon storage URLs, internal actor relations, or library IDs are exposed or saved in replay snapshots. ## Delete a category and its children Deleting a category also deletes its child categories. If any category in that subtree contains a nondeleted product, the API returns `409 category_has_products` and leaves every category unchanged. Deleting a category subtree removes its direct template bindings in the same transaction. Deletion is a soft delete: names, parent IDs, brand IDs and historical product relationships are preserved. New categories can reuse the original paths, and the remaining sibling categories are reordered. Product content and status do not change; assets, templates and brands are not deleted. Deleted categories no longer appear in reads and cannot be assigned to products.

title: Product information templates
description: Manage fields, bindings and defaults while preserving product template versions.
markdown:
All paths use `/api/product`. Writes require a `manage` API Key Collaborator. ## Creating and updating To create a template, provide a name and at least one group. This example adds an optional color field: ```json { "name": "Catalog", "groups": [ { "name": "Basics", "fields": [ { "key": "color", "name": "Color", "type": "text" } ] } ] } ``` `POST /product-info-templates` returns `201`; `PATCH /product-info-templates/{id}` returns `200`. Both return template details and an `ETag`. Names allow 1–30 characters; descriptions allow up to 50. On update, omitting `groups` preserves the definition. Supplying `groups` replaces the complete definition. Keep existing group and field `id` values, and omit `id` for new groups and fields. Omitted existing groups and fields are soft-deleted.
Bindings, the default template, and versions - `boundBrandIds` and `boundCategoryIds` replace only the supplied binding dimension. Omitted arrays stay unchanged; each array allows up to 10,000 IDs. IDs must belong to the same library. When brands are selected, categories must belong to those brands. IDs bound to another template move to this template. - `isLibraryDefault: true` makes this template the library default. `false` clears the default only if this template is currently selected. Omission leaves it unchanged. - Every successful create or update saves a new version. Only `syncStrategy: "newOnly"` is supported; `syncAll` returns `422 validation_failed`. Existing products keep the version used at creation, including its field definitions and values.
`POST` supports safe retries with `Idempotency-Key`; updates can check the version with `If-Match`. See [Write conventions](./product-library-write-conventions). For all top-level parameters, see [Create a template](./product-library-reference#operation-createTemplate) and [Update a template](./product-library-reference#operation-updateTemplate). ## Groups `groups` contains 1–200 groups. A template may have at most 200 fields in total. | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | Required for an existing group, 1–128 characters, belonging to this template. Omit for a new group. | | `name` | string | Required, 1–128 characters. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed. | | `fields` | array | Required. Fields in the group, described below. | Existing groups keep their stored order; new groups append in the supplied order. Groups do not accept `sortOrder` or `isDefault`. The server assigns the default group, which cannot be deleted. ## Fields New fields require `key`, `name`, and `type`. Existing fields require `id`; omitted properties retain their values, except for `sortOrder`. | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | string | Required for an existing field, 1–128 characters, belonging to this group. Omit for a new field. | | `key` | string | Required for a new field, 1–64 characters. A unique, valid identifier; cannot change for existing fields. | | `name` | string | Required for a new field, 1–128 characters. | | `type` | string | Required for a new field. Supported types appear in the configuration table below. | | `required` | boolean | Optional. Defaults to `false` for a new field. | | `placeholder` | string or null | Optional, up to 255 characters. Defaults to `null` for a new field. | | `sortOrder` | integer | Optional, nonnegative. If omitted, uses the field's array position. | | `config` | object | Depends on the field type; see below. Defaults to `{}` for a new field, but must still meet that type's configuration requirements. | | `typeChangeConfirmed` | boolean | Optional. Set to `true` for an allowed type change that requires confirmation. |
System fields and update restrictions Creation seeds three protected fields: name, SKU, and main image. This leaves room for up to 197 custom fields. Replacement definitions must keep these field IDs, types, required flags, and configurations. Fields cannot move between groups. New fields must be custom fields and cannot use reserved system keys. `isSystemField` and `systemKey` cannot create or reassign system identities; preserve their values on update. Unknown group or field properties are rejected.
## Field configuration `config` depends on the field's `type`. For example, text fields use `{}`, while currency and choice fields need additional configuration.
View configuration for each field type | Field type | Configuration | | --- | --- | | `text`, `textarea`, `email`, `phone`, `url`, `color`, `date`, `dateRange` | Use `{}`. Other configuration properties are not accepted. | | `number` | Optional `unit`, a string. | | `currency` | Required `code` and `symbol` (nonempty strings), and `decimals` (an integer from 0 to 4). | | `richtext` | Required `mode`, either `html` or `delta`. | | `select`, `radio`, `checkbox` | Required, nonempty `options` array. Entries follow the table below; `value` must be unique. | | `image`, `file` | Optional `maxCount` (an integer of at least 1), `maxSizeMB` (a number greater than 0), and `accept` (an array of strings). | Each `options` entry contains: | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | string | Required, nonempty. The option's unique value. | | `label` | string | Required, nonempty. The display label. | | `sortOrder` | integer | Required, nonnegative. | | `archived` | boolean | Optional. Whether the option is archived. | System fields support `customPlaceholder`, an optional string of up to 255 characters. System brand and category fields do not accept custom options. Protected system fields cannot change their configuration. Empty and system configurations reject unknown properties. Other configuration and option validators strip unknown properties. Download the [OpenAPI JSON](/assets/developers/product-library/openapi.json) for the full machine-readable definition.
## Returned template definition Template details use `groups`; products use `templateDefinition.groups`. Both contain groups and fields. Products return the version pinned at creation, unchanged by later template edits or deletion. `templateDefinition` may be `null` when no template is assigned.
View returned group and field properties Each group always returns `id`, `name`, `fields`, and these read-only properties: | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `isDefault` | boolean | Whether this is the default group. | | `sortOrder` | integer | The group's order. | Each field always returns `id`, `key`, `name`, `type`, `required`, `placeholder`, `sortOrder`, `config`, and the following properties. The write-only parameter `typeChangeConfirmed` is not returned. | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `isSystemField` | boolean | Whether this is a system field. | | `systemKey` | string or null | System identity: `name`, `sku`, `brand`, `category`, `description`, or `mainImage`. `null` for custom fields. | `placeholder` may be `null`. Media references in configuration return safe preview information without storage paths or credentials. Reading a product's pinned template definition does not require `templates:read`.
## Preconditions and deletion `PATCH` and `DELETE` accept optional `If-Match`. Send the exact `ETag` returned when reading the template. A stale value returns `412 precondition_failed` without changing the template. If omitted, the later write takes precedence. `DELETE /product-info-templates/{id}` soft-deletes the template and removes brand and category bindings. Historical versions and product pins remain. Success returns `200` with the deleted ID and an `ETag`.
Deleting the default template and handling errors Deleting the library default requires the JSON field `replacementForLibraryDefault`: another live template ID in the same library, or `null` to clear the default. Omission returns `409 default_template_replacement_required`. Deleting a nondefault template does not require a body. Invalid definitions, references, protected field changes, or duplicate field keys return `422 validation_failed`. A duplicate live template name returns `409 name_in_use`. A missing template or one outside the current library returns `404 not_found`.

title: Product operations guide
description: Create, update, and publish products, preview assets, share products, and download or export files.
markdown:
Follow the operation you need, from creating a draft to publishing, previewing, sharing, and downloading products. All paths are relative to `https://open.musedam.cc/api/product`; see the [API reference](./product-library-reference) for complete parameters. ## Create a product Call `POST /products` with `products:create` permission to create a draft. Success returns `201`, product details in `data`, and a strong `ETag` response header. 1. Prepare the name, SKU, and any brand, category, or asset IDs to associate. 2. Supply `templateId` to choose a template, or use the resolution order below. 3. Complete the fields and then [publish the product](#publish-product). Creation does not accept `status` or `templateVersionId`.
Which fields can I create or update? | Field | Value | Create default / update behavior | | --- | --- | --- | | `name` | String, at most 255 characters | Empty name / preserve when omitted | | `spu` | String, at most 64 characters, or null | null; whitespace trims to null / preserve when omitted | | `description` | String or null | null / null clears | | `brandId`, `categoryId` | Positive integer or null | null / preserve when omitted; the resulting category must belong to the resulting brand | | `ownerUserId` | Same-team member ID or null | No owner / preserve when omitted, null clears | | `templateId` | Live same-library template ID or null | Explicit or resolved template / rejected on update | | `templateFields` | Object keyed by custom field ID | Empty / shallow merge, null clears one field | | `coverAssetId` | Library Asset ID or null | No explicit cover / null clears | | `imageAssetIds` | Array of Library Asset IDs | Empty / preserve when omitted, empty array clears; the first image becomes the cover unless `coverAssetId` is supplied | | `relatedAssetIds` | Array of Library Asset IDs | Empty / preserve when omitted, including legacy associations; empty array clears | The body accepts only these fields. API creator/updater attribution is separate from product ownership; the API key creator does not automatically become the owner.
What does a retried creation return for products and media? - Creation accepts `Idempotency-Key`, retained for 24 hours within the team, API key, and operation scope. See [creation and retries](./product-library-write-conventions). - Replay preserves the original non-media fields, business text, links, and ETag. Records store original media IDs, never storage URLs or signatures. - Media is checked again against current grants, product visibility, file validity, and the same current association slot. New associations are not added to the original result; detached media in structured custom values is also omitted. - Download properties still require product-read and product-download grants. Deleted or invisible products cannot reappear through replay; text and URL fields remain ordinary business data.
## Use templates and custom fields A new product saves the latest version of its resolved template. Interpret `templateFields` using the product's returned `templateDefinition`, not the template's current definition; later template edits or deletion do not change existing products' versions or values. Ordinary PATCH cannot switch a product's template. See [template management](./product-library-template-writes) for template creation, configuration, and bindings.
Which fields are in the product's template definition? `templateDefinition` is the version saved with the product, or null when no template is assigned. Reading it does not require `templates:read`. | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `groups` | Object array | Groups and their field definitions; see [template definition fields](./product-library-template-writes#template-definition) | `templateFields` is keyed by field ID from this definition, not by field name or key. Scalar values retain their JSON types; image and file values return arrays of [media objects](#product-media-fields).
How is a template chosen without templateId? - An explicitly supplied live `templateId` takes precedence. - If `templateId` is omitted or null and a non-null `categoryId` is supplied, resolve the category or ancestor binding, then that category's brand binding, then the library default. - If `categoryId` is omitted or null, only the library default is considered, even when `brandId` is supplied. - If none resolves, the product has no template. A missing or mismatched pinned version on an existing product returns an internal error; it does not select another version.
Custom field formats and asset limits | Field type | Input format | | --- | --- | | `number`, `currency` | JSON number | | `dateRange` | Ordered pair of date strings | | `checkbox` | Array of option values | | `image`, `file` | Array of FilePath IDs, or null | | `richtext` | String in HTML mode; `{ "ops": [...] }` in delta mode | - `templateFields` uses field IDs from the pinned version. Updates shallow-merge values; null clears the corresponding field. - Drafts may omit required fields, but submitted and merged values must satisfy type, option, and media constraints. Dates must be real calendar dates, including valid leap days; ranges must be ordered. Existing datetime and timezone forms remain supported. - Image/file fields follow the pinned count, size, and accepted-type settings. Image slots require image assets. - One request may reference at most 100 assets across the cover, images, related assets, and custom fields. These operations associate existing assets; they do not upload, download, or synchronize them.
## Update a product Call `PATCH /products/{id}` with `products:update` permission. Send only the fields to change; success returns `200`, product details, and a strong `ETag`. | Current state | Update requirements | | --- | --- | | Draft | Required values may be absent; supplied values must remain valid | | Published | Also requires `products:publish`; validates the complete product and preserves its published state | To avoid overwriting another update, first read the product and send its `ETag` unchanged in `If-Match`. A stale value returns `412 precondition_failed` without changing the product; see [concurrent updates and retries](./product-library-write-conventions).
Why can changing one field fail validation elsewhere? - PATCH and publication validate the entire result against the pinned template, including stored values you did not change. - A legacy invalid URL, email, or asset can cause `422 validation_failed`. Check `details[].field`, then correct that value in the same PATCH or through the browser before retrying. - Validation or transaction failure before commit rolls back fields and asset associations together. There is no partial update or removal of unrelated fields. - A committed update can still fail to return its response. Follow [write outcomes and recovery](./product-library-write-conventions#write-outcomes-and-audit-durability); a failed response alone does not establish a rollback.
## Publish or return to draft Call `PATCH /products/{id}/status` with either `{"status":"published"}` or `{"status":"draft"}`. Both `products:update` and `products:publish` are required, even when the requested state is unchanged. | Action | Validation and result | | --- | --- | | Publish | Checks the pinned required fields, types, options, and asset availability and limits; missing fields return `422` with field details | | First publication | Sets `publishedAt`; repeated publication preserves it | | Return to draft | Clears `publishedAt` and permits later incomplete draft edits | Name, SKU, and cover are required by default; the pinned template defines the actual requirements. Success returns product details and a new strong `ETag`; a stale optional `If-Match` returns `412` without changing the product. ## Delete products and handle errors Call `DELETE /products/{id}` with `products:delete`; a published product also requires `products:publish`. This soft deletion returns `200`, `data: {"id": 123}`, and a new strong `ETag`; repeating it returns `404`. Deletion accepts optional `If-Match` with the same validation as updates. | Error | What to do | | --- | --- | | `422 validation_failed` | Check optional `details[].field` and `message`; correct fields or foreign, deleted, or invalid references | | `409 sku_in_use` | Choose another SKU; soft-deleted products still participate in uniqueness checks | | `404 not_found` | Check the product ID and library; foreign, deleted, and missing products share this response | ## Preview and download links Use `previewUrl` to display product media. For originals, check `downloadUrl` or use the download operations below; preview access does not establish download permission. | Link | Availability | Maximum service-issued lifetime | | --- | --- | --- | | Derived preview | Appropriate viewing permission | 3600 seconds | | Original-image preview fallback | Images only; may also be returned to `view_only` | 300 seconds | | `downloadUrl` | Resolvable, visible association; `usable` or higher plus `products:read` and `products:download` | 300 seconds | Every service-issued link is also bounded by the API key's expiry. Fetch product data again after a link expires; do not persist signed URLs as asset identifiers.
Which fields do covers, images, and related assets return? `cover` is one media object, or null when there is no cover. `images`, `relatedAssets`, and custom image/file values are arrays of media objects. | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | Integer or null | ID returned by asset lookup (FilePath ID), not an AssetObject ID or product-asset association ID | | `name`, `mimeType` | String or null | File name and MIME type | | `size` | String or null | Decimal byte count, such as `"2048"`; never a JSON number | | `width`, `height`, `duration` | Number or null | Media dimensions and duration | | `previewUrl` | URL or null | Preview for display; null when unavailable | | `downloadUrl` | URL or null; may be omitted | Original file URL; availability is described above | | `downloadUrlExpiresAt` | Timestamp or null; may be omitted | Download URL expiry in RFC 3339 format |
How do missing links, legacy media, and external previews behave? - Non-image assets only return derived previews. Original PDFs, archives, and documents never serve as preview fallbacks. Library asset lookup and template configuration contain previews only. - Missing download permission or an unresolved association omits `downloadUrl` and `downloadUrlExpiresAt`. With permission but an unavailable original, those values may be null. - Stored external DAM thumbnails or previews are returned only to API keys without expiry, after excluding known original URLs. The provider controls their lifetime; short expiry and provider-signature validation are not guaranteed. - For an API key with `expiresAt`, an external preview whose expiry cannot be verified is null. Signature-like query parameters are not a trusted expiry source. - Service-issued URLs keep the limits above. Signing failure never falls back to a raw storage URL.
## Sharing, downloads, and history Choose an operation by its purpose. The roles and permissions below are checked on each request. | Purpose | Required role and permissions | | --- | --- | | Create a share | `usable` or higher, `products:read` and `products:share`; enabling downloads also requires `products:download` | | Download or export | `usable` or higher, `products:read` and `products:download`; `usable` can access published products only | | Revoke a team share | `manage` and `products:share`; does not additionally require `products:read` | | List team history | `manage` and `products:history`; does not additionally require `products:read` | ### Create and revoke shares Use `POST /product-shares` for a fixed selection of 1–100 published products. It returns an absolute access URL; visitors need no login or API key. | Parameter | Values | | --- | --- | | `expiresInDays` | 7, 30, 90, or null for no expiry | | `allowDownload` | Whether visitors may download | | `accessCode` | Optional, exactly four digits | Shares show current product content; unpublished or deleted products are hidden. A share belongs to the team and survives its creator key's expiry, deactivation, revocation, or permission changes; call `DELETE /product-shares/{id}` to stop access. ### Download originals 1. Call `GET /products/{id}/download-assets` for candidate `assetKey` and `downloadable` values. This step returns no media URLs and creates no download record. 2. Call `POST /product-downloads` with `kind: "assets"` and `productIds`. Select files with `assetKeys`, or omit it to select all originals. 3. One file returns the original attachment; multiple files return a ZIP. Missing originals remain unavailable. For one file, you can also call `GET /products/{id}/download-assets/{assetKey}`. Encode the candidate key as a path segment; it is not an asset ID. Every retrieval checks current permission. ### Export product tables Call `POST /product-downloads` with `kind: "export"`. Choose `xlsx` (default), `csv`, or `json` as `format`; `assetKeys` is not accepted. - `locale` defaults to `zh-CN` and changes only system labels and statuses, not custom labels or values. - `includeAssetUrls` defaults to true. Table links point to the single-file endpoint requiring a Bearer header, without embedding credentials; clicking a link does not send that header. - Create a share for browser access without API credentials. Machine synchronization uses stable product-read fields, not localized table exports. ### Query records and retry downloads Downloads and exports return a record ID in `X-Download-Record-Id`. `requested` means accepted, not transferred or saved locally; a detected preparation or transfer failure after acceptance marks the record `failed`, and retries do not reset its state. Use `GET /product-shares` or `GET /product-downloads` for team history. Omit `productId` for the whole team or provide one product ID for matching operations; both accept `page` and `pageSize` and return newest first.
Which fields are in a record's product snapshots? The `products` array in share and download records preserves product details at the time of the operation. Later product edits do not update it. | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | Positive integer | Product ID | | `name` | String | Product name at the time of the operation | | `spu` | String or null | SKU at the time of the operation |
Which fields are in a download record's file snapshots? A download record's `files` array preserves file details when the operation is first accepted. | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | String | File snapshot identifier | | `productId` | Positive integer | Associated product ID | | `name` | String | File name at the time of the operation |
How can I retry one download without creating another record? - Reuse the same `Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours, scoped to the team, API key, and operation. POST downloads and single-file GET have separate scopes. - Matching retries reuse the first record and snapshot, but authorize again, read current content, and transfer it. File bytes are not cached. - Changing input under the same key returns `409`. Omitting the key, using a new key, or retrying after retention creates a new operation; deduplication is not permanent. - Before attachment delivery starts, errors keep their specific codes. Committed or replayed records also include `mutationOutcome`; keep the original idempotency key when retrying an accepted operation. - Ordinary product reads, previews, and direct storage `downloadUrl` access do not enter business download history.
Which records appear in team history? - Browser operations and other API keys in the team are included. The current key or creator does not implicitly narrow results. - Filtering by product still returns the complete operation, including its other products and files. - Key ID and name snapshots preserve attribution after later key changes. - History endpoints accept only `productId`, `page`, and `pageSize`; unknown or repeated parameters are rejected.

title: Product synchronization
description: Synchronize with cursors and checkpoints, and reconcile invisible products.
markdown: Ordinary `GET /api/product/products?page=...` listings are for browsing, not synchronization. Use `GET /api/product/products?sync=true` for both the first full copy and every incremental cycle. All requests require `products:read` and use the same role and library visibility rules as ordinary product reads. ## Synchronization steps 1. Start with `sync=true`, optional `pageSize` (default 20, capped at 100), and optional product filters `search`, `brandId`, `categoryId`, and `status`. Omit `updatedAfter` for a full sync. For an incremental cycle, set it to the previous completed cycle's `syncedUntil` string without changing its precision. 2. Merge returned products by `id` and `updatedAt`, keeping the newer version. 3. Follow `pagination.nextCursor` with `sync=true&cursor=...` until it is null. An empty data page can still have a next cursor when selected products became invisible while preparing the response. Continue following that cursor. 4. Save the completed cycle's `syncedUntil` unchanged as the next checkpoint. Do not substitute the final product's timestamp. Sync pagination has this shape: ```json { "pageSize": 20, "syncedUntil": "2026-10-08T12:00:00.123456Z", "nextCursor": null, "hasMore": false } ``` The cursor is opaque and versioned. It retains the exact lower bound, upper bound, last `(updatedAt, id)` position, page size, and filters. A subsequent request may omit filters, page size, and `updatedAfter`; the saved values apply. If repeated, they must match the original cycle (equivalent RFC 3339 offsets are accepted for the lower bound). Changing any of them, using a cursor with another API key or role, malformed cursor data, duplicate sync parameters, or supplying `page` returns `422 validation_failed`. Restart the cycle after changing keys or roles. `cursor` and `updatedAfter` require `sync=true`; unsupported sync values are also rejected. `sync=false` uses the ordinary browsing list. `updatedAfter` accepts RFC 3339 timestamps with a timezone (`Z` or numeric offset) and zero to six fractional digits. Invalid calendar dates, invalid offsets, precision beyond six digits, and a lower bound later than the safe upper bound return `422 validation_failed`. Returned checkpoints and sync product `updatedAt` values use UTC with exactly six fractional digits. Preserve those strings in storage; JavaScript Date cannot retain their full precision. ## Handle updates during synchronization Each cycle reads `[updatedAfter, syncedUntil)`, ordered by `updatedAt` and then `id`, both ascending. The lower bound is inclusive and the upper bound exclusive. An update exactly at `syncedUntil` belongs to the next cycle. The first page sets the upper bound to the server time minus 30 seconds; every later page uses the same bound. The 30-second window excludes recent updates that have not yet committed. Transactions lasting longer than this window can still affect synchronization completeness. Synchronization uses at-least-once delivery: products updated again during a cycle may appear on later pages more than once. Merge by ID and update time, and retry a failed page with its original cursor. Sync timestamps retain microsecond precision. Each response rechecks key permissions and current product visibility. Deleted or newly invisible products are omitted without failing the whole page, and the cursor still advances. Deleting products from earlier pages does not cause later products to be skipped. ## Handle deleted or invisible products `POST /api/product/products/visibility` accepts only this body: ```json { "ids": [42, 43] } ``` It accepts zero to 100 positive integer product IDs (maximum 2147483647), retaining input order and duplicate occurrences. Its `data` contains no product content: ```json [ { "id": 42, "visibility": "visible" }, { "id": 43, "visibility": "not_visible" } ] ``` For published-only roles, draft, deleted, foreign, and missing IDs all receive the same `not_visible` value. Editable and manageable roles may also see drafts. Only submitted IDs are returned; there is no removal feed or draft discovery endpoint. Call this periodically for IDs already stored by the integration, for example after each completed cycle. Invalid bodies, noninteger IDs, unknown body fields, and batches over 100 return `422 validation_failed`. When an ID is `not_visible`, remove the corresponding product from local storage.

title: App authentication
description: Authorize third-party applications and manage enterprise API keys.
markdown:
## Overview

Third-party applications can access enterprise Open APIs after an enterprise administrator enables and authorizes the application. Use appId and appSecretKey to manage API keys, then use those keys to call the core APIs.

## Basics

### Base URLs

- **Mainland China**: https://open.musedam.cc/api/apps
- **Overseas**: https://open.musedam.ai/api/apps

### Authentication

Use **HTTP Basic Authentication**:

- Combine appId and appSecretKey as `appId:appSecretKey` and Base64-encode the string.
- Add the HTTP header: `Authorization: Basic [Base64-encoded value]`.
- All application management requests must include this authentication.

**Authentication example:**

Given the following credentials:

- appId: `test_app_123`
- appSecretKey: `s3cr3t_k3y_456`

**Steps:**

1. Combine appId and appSecretKey: `test_app_123:s3cr3t_k3y_456`.
2. Base64-encode the string: `dGVzdF9hcHBfMTIzOnMzY3IzdF9rM3lfNDU2`.
3. Add the authentication header:

   ```text
   Authorization: Basic YOUR_BASE64_APP_CREDENTIALS
   ```

> **Note**: Request appId and appSecretKey from your MuseDAM account representative.

### Get an API key

**Endpoint**: `/exchange-api-key`

**Method**: POST

**Request body:**

```text
{
    "orgId":185
}
```

**Response**:

```json
{
    "code": 0,
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {
        "apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY",
        "expiresAt": "2055-08-19 16:13:25",
        "org": {
            "id": 185,
            "name": "Example team",
            "orgNo": "M000001",
            "orgFeeType": 4
        }
    },
    "traceId": "17555988913681722512"
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/apps/exchange-api-key' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic YOUR_BASE64_APP_CREDENTIALS' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "orgId":185
}'
```

---

### Refresh an API key

**Endpoint**: `/refresh-api-key`

**Method**: POST

**Request body:**

```text
{
    "oldApiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}
```

**Response**:

```json
{
    "code": 0,
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {
        "apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY",
        "expiresAt": "2055-08-19 18:22:18"
    },
    "traceId": "17555989381206489704"
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/apps/refresh-api-key' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic YOUR_BASE64_APP_CREDENTIALS' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "oldApiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}'
```

---

### Revoke an API key

**Endpoint**: `/revoke-api-key`

**Method**: POST

**Request body:**

```text
{
    "apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}
```

**Response**:

```json
{
    "code": 0,
    "message": "OK",
    "result": true,
    "traceId": "17555989381206489704"
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/apps/revoke-api-key' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic YOUR_BASE64_APP_CREDENTIALS' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}'
```

---

### Query installation status

**Endpoint**: `/get-install-status?orgId=185`

**Method**: GET

**Response**:

```json
{
    "code": 0,
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {
        "appId": "app_4f8c6e9d2b7a",
```

### List all installations

**Method**: GET

title: MCP overview
description: Connect AI clients to your asset library through Model Context Protocol.
markdown:
This guide explains how MCP clients such as Cursor, Claude Desktop, and custom clients connect to the MuseDAM production MCP service using **Streamable HTTP**.
MuseDAM MCP can also be used through a Skill. API documentation and downloads:
https://github.com/kang-oy/musedam-open-api.git

---

## Service overview

| Item | Description |
|-|-|
| Protocol | Model Context Protocol (MCP) |
| Capabilities | MuseDAM Open APIs exposed as MCP tools: asset search, upload, editing, tags, folders, shared link search, team information, and more |
| Authentication | A MuseDAM API key is required. See the API guide to obtain an `api_key` |

### Production endpoint and regions

| Environment | URL | Description |
|-|-|-|
| Production | `https://mcp-service.musedam.cc` | Defaults to Mainland China (`cn`); append `?region=overseas` for overseas accounts |

---

## Choose a connection method

Connect to the remote MCP service using Streamable HTTP, without deploying a local process:

| Method | Use case | API key delivery |
|-|-|-|
| **Streamable HTTP** | Client connects to a remote MCP service over HTTP | HTTP `Authorization` header, such as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` |

---

title: Connect MCP
description: Configure production MCP connections using Streamable HTTP.
markdown:
## Streamable HTTP

### How it works

- The MCP server runs as an HTTP service and supports concurrent clients.
- Clients communicate using standard HTTP requests and JSON-RPC.
- Suitable for remote deployment and multiple clients, such as Cursor URL connections or custom web clients.

### Endpoint and authentication

- **Path**: `/` (root)
- **Method**: `POST` (JSON-RPC requests)
- **Authentication**: Include the API key in the HTTP `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_MUSEDAM_API_KEY>`
- **Region**: Set the optional URL query parameter `?region=<region>`; defaults to `cn`.

### Production connection settings

**Production:**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "musedam": {
      "url": "https://mcp-service.musedam.cc?region=overseas",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MUSEDAM_API_KEY"
      },
      "name": "MuseDAM"
    }
  }
}
```

Mainland China defaults to `cn` and requires no query parameter. For overseas accounts, use `?region=overseas`, as shown in the English example.

### Configuration parameters

- **url**: Server address. Set the region with `?region=xxx` (optional; defaults to `cn`).

  - Values: `cn` (Mainland China, default), `overseas` (Overseas).
- **headers.Authorization**: Required authentication in `Bearer <api_key>` format.

Some clients use `serverUrl` instead of `url`. Follow your client's configuration format.

### Health check

The service provides a health check endpoint for operations and load balancer probes:

- **Path**: `GET /health_check`
- **Success**: HTTP 200; no response body is required.

Example:

- Production: `https://mcp-service.musedam.cc/health_check`

---

## Regions and APIs

| region | Description | MuseDAM Open API Base URL |
|-|-|-|
| `cn` | Mainland China (default) | `https://open.musedam.cc/api/muse` |
| `overseas` | Overseas | `https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse` |

These MCP tools access MuseDAM through the Open API. HTTP methods follow the corresponding API endpoints, using `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. For MCP, configure the key and region through connection settings.

---

title: MCP troubleshooting
description: Troubleshoot MCP authentication, connections, and tool calls.
markdown:
## Connection and tool call issues

**Q: Streamable HTTP returns 401?**  

A: Ensure the request includes `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` and the key is correct and has not expired.

**Q: Where do I get an API key?**  

A: Request one from MuseDAM or your administrator. The MCP service does not provide a default key.

**Q: Why are api_key and region no longer tool parameters?**  

A: They are now managed through connection settings: headers and query parameters for HTTP. This keeps credentials out of individual tool arguments.

**Q: A tool call fails with “Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 16”, and the MCP server receives no request?**  

A: The error occurs in **Cursor**, before `tools/call` is sent. Cursor may have generated invalid JSON when serializing tool `arguments`, for example for `musedam_search_assets`, or encountered a JSON parsing error while processing the call.

Suggested steps:

1. Retry in Cursor or start a new conversation. If needed, report the client-side JSON error to Cursor, noting that the server received no request.
2. For custom MCP clients, ensure `arguments` uses **valid JSON with double quotes** and that the entire `tools/call` message is parseable.

title: Business use cases
description: Connect MuseDAM to CMS, commerce, and marketing workflows.
markdown:
## CMS integration

### Scenario

Let editors find and use MuseDAM assets directly inside your CMS. Keep assets centrally managed while the CMS maintains the relationship between content and assets.

### Integration approach

> CMS editor → Backend → MuseDAM: search assets, return previews, store asset IDs, refresh links before publishing.

**Implementation notes**

- **Select assets**: Embed a custom picker in the editor and call `/search-assets` ([asset search](./search)) through your backend. Keep the API key on the server.
- **Save references**: Store asset IDs in content records. Before publishing, use `/assets-by-ids` ([batch retrieval](./assets)) to refresh URLs or copy files to CMS storage. Do not treat temporary download links as permanent content URLs.
- **Keep content current**: Use `/material-automation-subscribe` ([asset event subscriptions](./events)) for metadata changes, version changes, and deletions. Subscriptions are team-wide; the CMS filters by linked asset IDs and decides whether to update or unpublish content.

## E-commerce product management

### Scenario

Manage product images and videos in MuseDAM. Your product system maps assets to SKUs and publishes content tailored to each storefront and channel.

### Integration approach

> Product system → MuseDAM → Product system → Storefronts: upload assets, link SKUs, search and process images, publish through channel APIs.

**Implementation notes**

- **Organize assets**: Optionally create a folder per SKU with `/create-folder` and upload product assets with `/upload-assets`. Store the mapping between SKUs, folder IDs, and asset IDs in your product system.
- **Adapt to channels**: Use `/processed-public-links` ([image processing and delivery](./analysis)) to retrieve correctly sized images. DAT must be enabled and assets must already have public links; this endpoint does not create a public address for an asset without one.
- **Update listings**: Use `/material-automation-subscribe` ([asset event subscriptions](./events)) for completed ingestion, metadata changes, version changes, and deletions. Filter events by asset IDs linked to SKUs, fetch current content, and call channel APIs. Handle deletions according to your unpublishing rules and track publishing status and version references in your system.

## Marketing asset distribution

### Scenario

Maintain campaign assets in MuseDAM. A distribution service receives changes or runs scheduled searches, then publishes assets according to channel rules and tracks each delivery.

### Integration approach

> Distribution service → MuseDAM → Distribution service → Channels: subscribe via /material-automation-subscribe, receive events, retrieve assets, publish and track results.

**Implementation notes**

- **Choose a trigger**: Use `/material-automation-subscribe` ([asset event subscriptions](./events)) for timely updates, or scheduled `/search-assets` calls for batch delivery. After an event, fetch current details with `/assets-by-ids`; your system handles unpublishing deleted assets.
- **Select events and scope**: Use `/material-automation-event-types` to discover available events. Subscribe to `MATERIAL_INBOUND_COMPLETED`, `MATERIAL_METADATA_UPDATED`, `MATERIAL_VERSION_CHANGED`, and `MATERIAL_DELETED`; add `MATERIAL_ADDED_TO_FOLDER` when entering a campaign folder should trigger delivery. Subscriptions are team-wide, so your distribution service filters by campaign, folder, or asset mapping.
- **Deliver reliably**: Your service handles callback validation, event deduplication, queuing, and bounded retries to avoid duplicate publishing.
- **Track results**: Save asset IDs, channel content IDs, publishing status, and timestamps. Retrieve performance data from each channel and aggregate it in your system.
